prompt: Design a fitness training app for runners — track workouts, streaks, and personal records. It needs a home dashboard with today's workout and metrics, a workout library to browse and start guided runs, and a profile screen with goals and settings. Make it feel athletic, motivating, and modern.
title: Nike Run Coach

issues.description: Uses non-approved color tokens/classes ('bg-success-subtle', 'bg-warning-subtle') that are not in the provided token set. This violates the theme token discipline and can break consistency/contrast.

Static cards use shadow-sm and a hardcoded rounded-xl radius. Nike’s language calls for minimal hairline-border cards without soft shadow emphasis, and the universal rules require theme radius scale usage.

Button variants need explicit hover and active states that are clearly visible under the dark athletic system. The focus ring exists, but the styling should be verified against token-only surfaces and any undefined ring-offset dependency.
The switch has focus-ring utility classes but no visible hover/pressed state treatment. The thumb/track treatment is functional yet too bare for the stated interaction standards.

The home dashboard must have one dominant scoreboard/hero moment. The current composition reads as a standard app dashboard with many small modules instead of a single bold 'today' moment at hero scale.

The brief calls for a large quick-glance metrics row and streak status as a central action area. The screen should elevate the four key stats into one legible scoreboard row and reduce competing decorative chrome.

The workout library needs search plus a single filter control and a browsable workout list with distance, pace focus, intensity tags, and a fast launch step. This screen should be organized as a toolbar + table/list experience.
The guided run start flow should clearly show the selected workout summary, coaching cues, and a primary start button. The detail page needs to foreground those elements as the main action path.

The progress screen needs a branded chart moment that is the hero of the section, with a matching chart title and unit. The current layout should make the chart larger and the records table more explicit.
The personal records portion should clearly show best 5K, 10K, longest run, and fastest pace with dates. Make the record table concrete and fully legible.

The settings screen must explicitly present weekly mileage goals, pace targets, notifications, units, and app preferences. Ensure these are grouped cleanly and represented with the requested control types.
The settings screen should feel like a premium app page, not a generic form stack. Reduce visual noise and keep secondary actions quiet so the profile area reads as designed.
The screen is rendered on a white background with soft gray cards, which breaks the required dark-mode, athletic Nike look and loses the high-contrast brand identity.
The page has excessive whitespace and several loosely grouped blocks, so the today's workout does not read as one dominant moment.
The activity feed is generic and partially off-tone; it should use product-specific running data and coaching language, not dashboard-style social updates.
The settings screen is almost entirely white with minimal contrast, conflicting with the dark-mode-only brief and Nike design language.
The top module and surrounding settings sections feel repetitive and template-like, with multiple similar white panels stacked without a clear dominant focus.
Some labels read generic ('Your setup', 'Continue') and the screen could be more specific to running goals, pace targets, units, and notifications.
The stat row includes calories, which is not one of the requested performance metrics and makes the screen feel less focused on running records.
There is a large empty gap between the summary stats and the chart, creating a broken rhythm and diluting the page hierarchy.
The records table toolbar resembles an admin dashboard with search, filter, and new controls; it overuses card/table scaffolding rather than a fitness-forward composition.
The workout detail screen is sparse and underdeveloped, with a lot of empty white space and no strong athletic hero moment.
The screen lacks the required dark, bold Nike treatment and instead feels like a neutral web page.
The copy is acceptable but too restrained; it should be more concrete and action-oriented with clearer coaching cues and session summary details.
The library is dominated by a repetitive 3-column card grid, which violates the anti-uniform-card guidance and feels assembled from a template.
The cards have large empty interior areas and weak hierarchy, so the browsing section does not feel dense or legible enough for quick selection.
The browse section needs sharper, more specific run metadata and a more Nike-like voice to better fit the product brief.

reviewResult.summary: The build is directionally on-brand and domain-relevant, but it does not yet meet the composition and token standards for approval. The biggest misses are the lack of a true hero-scale scoreboard on Home, underdeveloped workout-library and workout-detail flows, and a progress screen that needs a more dominant branded chart moment. There are also token-discipline issues in shared components that should be corrected before approval.
requiredFixes: src/components/Badge.jsx: Replace non-token classes like bg-success-subtle and bg-warning-subtle with approved theme tokens (e.g. bg-success/10 text-success, bg-warning/10 text-warning) and add a visible focus/active treatment only if the badge is interactive.

src/components/Card.jsx: Remove shadow-sm from static cards and use the theme radius scale instead of hardcoded rounded-xl; keep panels minimal with hairline borders to match Nike’s dark athletic language.

src/components/Button.jsx: Ensure every variant has a visible hover/active state that stays within token discipline, and add a focus-visible ring-offset token if the current utility depends on an undefined background token.

src/components/Switch.jsx: Add hover and pressed states plus a clearly visible focus ring, and verify the switch thumb/track contrast uses theme tokens only; current implementation lacks the required hover/active affordances.

src/screens/home-dashboard.jsx: Make the Today dashboard’s dominant moment unmistakable at hero scale with a large full-bleed workout moment or scoreboard, and keep adjacent sections on different surfaces; avoid stacking multiple small cards and icon clutter.

src/screens/home-dashboard.jsx: Reduce the dense icon import/use pattern and present the four key metrics as a single large scoreboard row with tabular numbers, distinct labels, and accent deltas that match the brief.

src/screens/workout-library.jsx: Add the required single filter control alongside search and a primary action in a clear toolbar, and render the workouts in a dense, table-like browsable list with distance, pace focus, intensity tags, and status.

src/screens/workout-detail.jsx: Expand the guided run detail into a focused start flow with workout summary, coaching cues, and one dominant primary start button; make sure the detail fields from the brief are visibly represented.

src/screens/progress-records.jsx: Give the progress screen a branded chart moment with a real title and unit that matches the plotted metric, plus a clear personal-record table with dates and progress deltas; the chart should be the hero of the section.

src/screens/profile-settings.jsx: Replace any nonessential chrome with a clean settings layout that explicitly covers weekly mileage goals, pace targets, notification preferences, units, and dark-mode app settings using select/toggle controls only where specified.

src/screens/profile-settings.jsx: Keep control counts restrained and make the form feel premium rather than templated; avoid duplicating generic settings scaffolding and ensure the profile screen reads as a complete app page with quiet secondary actions.

home-dashboard: Convert the page to Nike dark mode with a black background, white typography, and a single volt hero moment; remove the large white canvas and make the hero/workout area full-bleed or visibly dark to match the brand and brief.

home-dashboard: Make the today's workout treatment the dominant moment with a clear planned session summary and one primary black/volt CTA; reduce the oversized empty whitespace above the chart and between sections.

home-dashboard: Replace the generic activity feed items and non-product-relevant names with Nike Run Coach-specific workout/recovery items, and tighten the bottom nav to look like mobile app chrome rather than desktop website navigation.
profile-settings: Rework the profile screen to match dark-mode Nike styling; the current all-white settings layout and pale cards conflict with the product brief and design language.

profile-settings: Add clearer goals/settings hierarchy with specific running controls only (weekly mileage goal, pace target, units, notifications); remove the unrelated workout list-style module at the top and make the primary action a filled black button aligned to the profile context.

progress-records: Change the screen from a generic metric dashboard into a records-focused view with best 5K/10K/longest run/fastest pace and dates; the current top stat row includes calories, which is off-brief and makes the screen feel like a template.
progress-records: Reduce the large empty gap between the stat row and the chart, and make the chart section feel more intentional with stronger labels and a more branded performance presentation.

progress-records: The personal records table uses a search + filter + new toolbar pattern that feels more like admin software than a fitness app; simplify the control set and keep only the single filter control required by the brief.

workout-detail: Replace the sparse white layout with a proper workout detail/start flow using dark mode, a clear summary, coaching cues, and one dominant full-bleed or statement section; the current center-aligned content is too empty and low-energy.

workout-detail: Remove the secondary outlined 'Preview route' style control or demote it further; the screen should favor one strong primary start action and avoid scaffold-like dual-button treatment.

workout-library: The library grid is too card-heavy and repetitive for the card budget/composition rules; convert to a tighter divided list or more varied layout with one dominant filter/search toolbar and less empty card surface.

workout-library: Add more explicit browse copy and ensure each run card includes the required duration, distance, pace focus, and intensity tag in a more compact, legible hierarchy; the current cards are overly sparse and read as unfinished placeholders.
